byTheNumbers.title: The year in numbers
byTheNumbers.standfirst: 1.4 billion people, nearly all with electricity at home, 82 mobile subscriptions for every 100, and 43 in 100 online.

items.title: Population
items.summary: India's population was about 1.40 billion in 2020.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Population, total
Our World in Data: Population (UN World Population Prospects, HYDE)

items.title: Life expectancy at birth
items.summary: A newborn in 2020 could expect to live about 70 years.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Life expectancy at birth, total (years)
Our World in Data: Life expectancy (UN World Population Prospects and other series)

items.title: Online
items.summary: About 43 percent of Indians used the internet in 2020, up from 7.5 percent in 2010.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Individuals using the Internet (% of population)
Our World in Data: Share of individuals using the internet

items.title: Mobile phones
items.summary: There were about 82 mobile subscriptions for every 100 people.

sources.label: World Bank, World Development Indicators: Mobile cellular subscriptions (per 100 people)

items.title: Electricity at home
items.summary: About 96.5 percent of the population had access to electricity, up from 51 percent in 1995.

items.title: Infant deaths
items.summary: About 28 of every 1,000 babies died before their first birthday.

byTheNumbers.scarcityNote: Literacy and household size were not found for 2020: the census had been taken in 2011 and was due in 2021.

foodAndKitchen.title: Food and the kitchen
foodAndKitchen.standfirst: Goa became the first state with a tap-water connection in every household.

items.title: A tap in every home
items.summary: On 10 October 2020 Goa was declared the first 'Har Ghar Jal' state, with tap water in every household.

foodAndKitchen.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2020 meals, kitchen costs or retail prices.

items.title: Handmade masks
items.summary: Self-help groups and tailors made cloth and khadi masks during the lockdown.

items.title: Working from home
items.summary: Office workers moved to casual clothes at home.

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.standfirst: The lockdown left millions without work and without a way home.

items.title: The economy contracts
items.summary: India's GDP contracted 23.9 percent in the first quarter of the 2020-21 financial year, reported on 31 August.

items.title: Walking home
items.summary: Migrant workers left jobless by the lockdown were seen walking or cycling hundreds of kilometres to their home villages, and from 1 May the railways ran 'Shramik Special' trains for stranded migrants; on 8 May 16 migrant workers were killed by a goods train near Aurangabad.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

workAndWages.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2020 wage rates or the number of jobs lost.

schoolAndChildhood.title: Growing up
schoolAndChildhood.standfirst: Schools shut in March and lessons moved to phones.

items.title: School at a screen
items.summary: Schools were shut, and the Unlock 5.0 guidelines of 30 September 2020 preferred online learning where possible.

schoolAndChildhood.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced 2020 counts of children affected or with phone access.

gettingAround.title: Getting around
gettingAround.standfirst: Trains and buses stopped, then started again in stages.

items.title: The lockdown
items.summary: From 25 March 2020 passenger trains, flights and metros stopped for the national lockdown.

sensitivity.note: This item touches on war, famine, epidemic disease or disaster.

items.title: Shramik Special trains
items.summary: From 1 May 2020 special trains carried migrant workers back to their home states.

items.title: Delhi Metro restarts
items.summary: The Delhi Metro resumed services in September 2020 in stages.

items.title: Flights resume
items.summary: Domestic flights restarted on 25 May 2020 under restrictions.

keepingInTouch.title: Keeping in touch
keepingInTouch.standfirst: Zoom and Google Meet became the usual way to meet relatives, attend school and hold work meetings.

items.title: Video calls
items.summary: Zoom and Google Meet became the usual way to meet relatives, attend school and hold work meetings.

items.title: Aarogya Setu
items.summary: The government's Aarogya Setu app, launched in April 2020, tracked contacts and gave health updates.

items.title: TikTok banned
items.summary: The government banned TikTok and dozens of other Chinese apps in June 2020.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Restrictions on TikTok in India

items.title: WhatsApp groups
items.summary: Families and neighbourhoods shared news and forwards on WhatsApp groups.

healthAndMedicine.title: Health and medicine
healthAndMedicine.standfirst: India confirmed its first case on 30 January, and passed one million cases on 17 July.

items.title: The first case
items.summary: India's first case of COVID-19 was reported on 30 January 2020 in Thrissur, Kerala, among students returning from Wuhan; daily cases peaked in mid-September at over 90,000.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

items.title: One million cases
items.summary: India passed one million confirmed COVID-19 cases on 17 July 2020.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

leisureAndFun.title: Evenings, weekends and festivals
leisureAndFun.standfirst: Doordarshan began re-running Ramayan from 28 March 2020 and it drew record viewership.

items.title: Ramayan on TV again
items.summary: Doordarshan began re-running Ramayan from 28 March 2020 and it drew record viewership.

items.title: IPL in the UAE
items.summary: The 2020 IPL was played in the UAE from September to November, without spectators, and Mumbai Indians won.

items.title: Streaming
items.summary: Films and series on Netflix, Hotstar and Amazon Prime were watched more during the lockdown.

items.title: Olympics postponed
items.summary: The Tokyo Olympics were postponed to 2021.

spotlight.title: Lockdown life and paying by phone
spotlight.standfirst: On 24 March the Prime Minister announced a lockdown for 1.38 billion people, and in the months that followed payments by phone grew by four-fifths.

items.title: The Janata Curfew
items.summary: A 14-hour voluntary curfew was observed on 22 March 2020, two days before the lockdown.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

items.title: The lockdown
items.summary: On the evening of 24 March 2020 the Government ordered a 21-day nationwide lockdown from midnight for the entire 1.38 billion population, closing all services and shops except pharmacies, hospitals, banks, grocery shops and other essential services, with only work from home allowed.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

items.title: Extended, then unlocked
items.summary: The lockdown was extended on 14 April to 3 May, on 1 May to 17 May and on 17 May to 31 May; services resumed in stages from 8 June, and Unlock 1.0 ran from 1 to 30 June, followed by monthly phases through Unlock 7.0 in December.

sensitivity.note: This item concerns the pandemic and its toll.

items.title: Payments by phone
items.summary: UPI recorded 1.14 billion transactions in October 2019 and 2.07 billion in October 2020; in all of 2019 it handled about 10.8 billion.

items.title: A system for every bank
items.summary: UPI began as a pilot on 11 April 2016 with 21 member banks, and by 2022 it linked 304.

spotlight.scarcityNote: We could not find sourced counts of small shops accepting UPI or smartphone ownership, so the payment growth is shown only in national totals.
